title: Do you drive a BMW? See if your car is subject to an urgent recall over fire risk. - Newsday
text:

 Wallet Watch Do you drive a BMW? See if your car is subject to an urgent recall over fire risk.
 BMW is recalling more than 700,000 vehicles due to a risk ​of fire while cars are parked and turned ​off.  Credit: dpa/picture alliance via Getty I/picture alliance
 November 16, 2026 1:31 pm Share BMW is recalling 720,796 cars over a faulty water pump that could increase fire risk, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration recall alert.
 An NHTSA consumer alert issued on Friday advises owners of the recalled vehicles to park their cars outside, away from other buildings and cars until BMW develops a fix for the water pump. BMW is working to complete a remedy for the water pump that will be available to consumers for free at BMW dealerships.
 There are seven BMW dealerships on Long Island according to the company's dealer locator.  
 A BMW spokesperson told Newsday in an emailed statement they have no details on the timing of the remedy to share at this time.
 The problem in the car models stems from an improperly sealed electrical conductor that may be exposed to water and short-circuit, increasing the risk of fire. The NHTSA report said the water pump can develop a short circuit when the ignition is off, so the conductor could short-circuit even while the vehicle is parked.

 The recall applies to 14 different BMW models manufactured between 2012 and 2018. BMW dealers were notified about the recall on Nov. 4. Notification letters are expected to be mailed to vehicle owners in December.
 The NHTSA notice states that recalled vehicle identification numbers (VINs) will be searchable on NHTSA.gov beginning Dec. 25. Models listed on the NHTSA’s recall notice include:
 2012-2016 BMW 3 Series
 2012-2016 BMW 5 Series
 2012–2015 BMW X1
 2012-2016 BMW Z4
 2013-2017 BMW X3
 2014-2016 BMW 2 Series coupe
 2014–2016 BMW 3 Series sport wagon
 2014-2016 BMW 328xi Gran Turismo
 2014-2016 BMW 4 Series convertible
 2014-2016 BMW 4 Series coupe
 2015-2016 BMW 2 Series convertible
 2015-2016 BMW 4 Series gran coupe
 2015-2018 BMW X4
 2016-2018 BMW X5 xDrive40e
 BMW issued a recall for these same models in 2024 because of water pump issues. According to an NHTSA report, the company installed a protective shield to divert fluid from the electrical conductor and, if necessary, replaced the pump or wire harness. Cars repaired under the last recall notice are still subject to the Nov. 4 notice and will need further repairs.
